claim: React Router has three modes; every mode supports any architecture (SPA/SSR/static); framework mode wraps data mode with a Vite plugin so build/HMR/code-split assembly is done for you.
quote: Every mode supports any architecture and deployment target. Framework Mode wraps Data Mode with a Vite plugin to add type-safe routing, intelligent code splitting, and flexible rendering strategies.

claim: Library mode is a pure router with no compiler dependency, usable with Vite/webpack/Parcel as a static bundle; framework mode adds full-stack build tooling.
quote: React Router library mode doesn't depend on any compiler so it can be used with Vite, Parcel, webpack, etc.

claim: Match the mode to project needs: declarative for simple SPAs, data for routing plus data handling, framework for full-stack with type safety and SSR.
quote: The key is matching the mode to your project's needs: declarative for simple SPAs, data for apps that need routing plus data handling, and framework for full-stack development with type safety and SSR support.

claim: React Router framework mode offers a first-class SPA mode (ssr:false) that prerenders a shell and ships the app as static files, no server required.
quote: Single Page App (SPA) — React Router can be used as a SPA framework; with ssr:false it prerenders the shell and serves the app as static files.

claim: RSC framework mode in React Router is a non-stable preview, requires a server runtime (cannot run as static files), and does not yet support SPA mode or prerendering.
quote: SPA Mode, pre-rendering and custom build entries are not yet supported, but rest assured we plan on supporting these before a stable release.

claim: RSC is an architectural boundary not an optimization; highly interactive dashboards become mostly client-bound, collapsing the server-first advantage and making the architecture harder to reason about.
quote: highly interactive, client-heavy interfaces often require most components to be client-bound, resulting in an architecture that is harder to reason about than a traditional client-driven React application.

claim: TanStack Start SPA mode adds a prerendering step to generate a shell and pairs with server functions; initial document is rendered on the client.
quote: After enabling SPA mode, running a Start build will have an additional prerendering step afterwards to generate the shell.

claim: TanStack Start is TanStack Router plus server capabilities; if you know you will not need server features, use TanStack Router alone as a type-safe SPA router.
quote: If you know with certainty that you will not need server features, you may want to consider using TanStack Router alone, which is still a powerful and type-safe SPA routing upgrade.

claim: Next.js supports building SPAs with client-side data fetching and static routes, but through its own routing model.
quote: Next.js fully supports building Single-Page Applications (SPAs), which includes fast route transitions with prefetching, client-side data fetching, using browser APIs.

claim: Next.js static export generates an HTML file per route and can start as a static site/SPA before optionally upgrading to server features.
quote: Next.js enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application (SPA), then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server.

claim: Next.js is awkward for the SPA paradigm because its built-in page-based routing conflicts with the client-side routing SPAs rely on.
quote: Next.js is nearly incompatible with the SPA paradigm for one fundamental reason: routing... whereas the typical SPA relies on client-side routing.

claim: The React team points SPA projects at Vite; React+Vite wins for auth-gated pages where a brief loading state is fine and server complexity isn't justified.
quote: React + Vite wins for auth-gated pages where a brief loading state is acceptable and server complexity isn't justified.

claim: Vite is best for SPAs, dashboards, and internal tools; a Vite SPA with a client router and TanStack Query is a production-ready stack when crawlers don't matter.
quote: Vite is the best choice for SPAs, dashboards, and internal tools where speed and simplicity matter most.

claim: React Router is UI-first (URL to component) while TanStack Router is state-first (URL to state to data to UI) with type-safety and DX as priorities.
quote: React Router uses UI-first routing (URL → Component) while TanStack Router uses state-first routing (URL → State → Data → UI).

claim: Remix merged into React Router v7; Wouter is a ~12 KB minimalist router that overlaps but doesn't match RR/TanStack on nested routes, FS routing, and prefetch.
quote: Wouter is lightweight at 12 KB with a lot of functionality. However, it has overlaps with features that React Router provides such as nested routes, file-based route generation, and automatic route prefetching.

claim: Next.js fatigue is a named 2026 trend driven by hydration debugging, RSC security incidents, and complexity, pushing internal-tool teams toward Vite SPAs with faster dev/build times.
quote: vulnerabilities including unauthenticated remote code execution through insecure deserialization in React Server Components affecting every Next.js App Router app with server actions.

claim: TanStack Router is a purpose-built type-safe client-side router; TanStack Start is the same repo's server layer on top.
quote: TanStack Router is the client-side routing library; TanStack Start is TanStack Router plus server capabilities.

claim: Wouter is a minimalist ~12 KB React router.
quote: A minimalist-friendly ~2.1KB routing for React and Preact.

claim: Next.js is the 2026 default for new full-stack admin apps with App Router, Server Components, and integrated routing/API/SSR — the key qualifier being full-stack.
quote: Next.js is the default for new full-stack apps in 2026 — App Router, Server Components, integrated routing + API + SSR.
